architecture_decision_notes: Selected the existing OSS validation layer. It handles the user's broad structure request while preventing unsafe omissions around direct import and hybrid modules.
architecture_theory_sources: Ports-and-adapters style boundary as local policy: core platform models must not depend on third-party framework internals
architecture_tradeoff_notes: Repository structures converge around separated agent lifecycle, tools/providers, state/checkpoints, product packages, and runtime/sandbox boundaries. Local policy favors adopting those as contracts first, not copying source.
code_reference_notes: Implementation follows existing dataclass/lightweight validation style, JSON CLI command style, and unittest structure.

folder_structure_options.decision: Selected because OSS provenance and adoption logic belongs beside dependency evaluation.
Rejected because no standalone lab or cloned framework is needed.
Rejected because OSS pattern provenance should not be mixed with agent orchestration contracts.

folder_structure_decision_notes: Source goes under agent-platform/src/agent_platform/oss, config under agent-platform/configs/open-source, tests under agent-platform/tests.
folder_semantics_notes: The oss module owns open-source dependency scoring and structure pattern adoption gates.
maintainability_notes: Keep the validator deterministic and dependency-free; future direct import or hybrid implementation must add explicit audit records and tests.
post_research_answers: Should code be cloned now: no, no specific feature target passed license/provenance/import gates.
Should another language be used now: no, but TypeScript/Rust/Go/C# are recorded as bounded hybrid options.
What is implemented now: Python-native pattern adoption validator, CLI, config, tests, and docs.
What remains for future work: direct feature import, provider adapter, sandbox sidecar, or productized package split only after a narrower target and audit.
